gaps.summary: Figma tokens fail WCAG AA 4.5:1 in places and AppTheme follows them as the source of truth. color/on-primary (#fdfdfd) on color/primary: 2.5:1 in Dark, True-dark and Slate, 2.4:1 in Dracula, 4.0:1 in Light. On color/danger: 3.1:1 Dracula, 3.7:1 Slate, 3.9:1 Light, 4.1:1 Dark and True-dark. color/text-secondary on color/app-background: 4.3:1 Light, 3.6:1 True-dark, 3.0:1 Dracula (Dark and Slate pass). color/text-muted: 2.5:1 Light, 3.0:1 True-dark, 4.0:1 Dracula, 4.4:1 Dark and Slate. Needs a Figma decision; PRODUCT.md has no WCAG target yet. color/border as the only outline of a control (Seletor segmentado border and divider) is 1.2-1.6:1 against color/app-background, below the 3:1 non-text guideline; the labels and the check icon carry the state. color/primary and color/danger as text on color/context-menu-bg (Diálogo/Confirmação actions) in Light: 3.8:1 and 3.7:1; the other themes pass. Download states drawn with raw tokens on the chapter card (color/secondary-60 over color/app-background), below 4.5:1: color/warning 1.3:1 in Light; color/success 2.5:1 in Light and 3.1:1 in Dark and True-dark; color/danger 3.2:1 in Light, 3.5:1 in Dracula and 4.4:1 in Slate; color/text-secondary 2.3:1 in Dracula, 3.8:1 in True-dark and 4.1:1 in Light. Issue #93 colours these icons and status texts with theme.legible(), which reaches at least 5.4:1 on the card in every theme. color/primary as the download summary's action text on the card: 3.2:1 in Light. color/danger as delete-action labels on color/context-menu-bg in Light: 3.9:1 for the selection bar and as drawn over the page, about 3.5:1 for sheets over the modal barrier in code, 3.7:1 for the dialog over the scrim. In Dark, True-dark and Slate the dialog panel is nearly the colour of the scrimmed background, so only the color/text-10 border (1.2-1.4:1) outlines it. Lilac pairings (snackbar, tertiary) use color/on-lilac (#000212, AppPalette.onLilac in code), 6.4:1 on color/lilac. Components from issue #126 (all measured by computing the pairs from the variable values): the Interruptor/Item knob in color/on-primary on the color/primary track is 2.5:1 in Dark, True-dark and Slate, 2.4:1 in Dracula and 4.0:1 in Light (non-text guideline is 3:1); the off track color/border against color/app-background is 1.2-1.6:1 and the off knob color/text-secondary on that track is 1.9:1 in Dracula (3.7-4.6:1 elsewhere); Esqueleto color/text-10 against the background is 1.2-1.35:1 (decorative placeholder, no text); the Cartão de chamada note in color/text-secondary on the card is 2.3:1 in Dracula, 3.8:1 in True-dark and 4.1:1 in Light (Dark and Slate pass), and the card title and description in color/text pass in every theme (10.3:1 or more); the Cartão de chamada and Vista de erro primary buttons repeat the color/on-primary on color/primary pairs above; the Diálogo/Confiar em certificado action color/primary on the color/context-menu-bg panel over color/app-background is 4.0:1 in Light (the 3.8:1 above for Diálogo/Confirmação is measured over the scrim, where the panel is darker). Logo from issue #144 (measured from the variable values; the logo is fixed brand art, so its colors do not change with the theme): the `#000212` body of `Marca/Logo` is 1.0-1.4:1 against color/app-background in Dark, True-dark, Dracula and Slate, so the dark shapes disappear into the page there and only the orange parts read (17.8:1 in Light, where the shapes show); `#f18522` is 2.2:1 on color/app-background in Light (5.5-8.1:1 in the other themes). Both are brand decisions for Figma, not fixed here. App lock frames (issue #127, computed from the variable values against color/app-background): color/primary as the grace-period section header and as the selected `Rádio/Item` ring and dot is 8.0:1 in Dark, 8.1:1 in True-dark, 7.0:1 in Slate, 5.9:1 in Dracula and 3.5:1 in Light (the text is below 4.5:1 in Light; the 3:1 non-text guideline holds); color/danger as the lock cover error text is 4.9:1 in Dark, 5.0:1 in True-dark, 4.8:1 in Slate, 4.5:1 in Dracula and 3.4:1 in Light; color/text-secondary as the cancelled message and as the unselected `Rádio/Item` ring is 7.1:1 in Slate, 5.0:1 in Dark, 4.3:1 in Light, 3.6:1 in True-dark and 3.0:1 in Dracula (the ring just meets 3:1 in Dracula); the `Interruptor/Item` rows repeat the knob and track pairs above; the authenticating button repeats color/on-primary on color/primary at 60% opacity. MFA frames (issue #128, computed from the variable values): color/danger as the error message and the Desativar label on color/app-background is 4.9:1 Dark, 5.0:1 True-dark, 4.8:1 Slate, 4.5:1 Dracula and 3.5:1 Light; the Caixa de seleção unmarked outline (color/text-secondary, non-text guideline 3:1) is 5.0:1 Dark, 7.1:1 Slate, 4.2:1 Light, 3.6:1 True-dark and 3.0:1 Dracula; the marked box repeats the color/on-primary on color/primary pairs above and color/primary against the background is 3.5:1 in Light and 5.9-8.1:1 elsewhere.

The #126 components are drawn in the intended Figma look, so code differs and each item is a code follow-up. Interruptor/Item: one row with an optional icon replaces AppSwitch (plain SwitchListTile, used in Settings and App lock), AppSwitchRow and ReaderSwitchRow. Esqueleto: code fills with onSurfaceVariant at 30% alpha (AppSkeleton, AppTextSkeleton), Figma uses color/text-10; the two skeleton widgets merge. Indicador de carregamento: code defaults to the Material indeterminate indicator with strokeWidth 2 and takes the size from the caller (20 in AppButton, 24 in the load-more footer, 40 in the profile page, none elsewhere); Figma names the 20/24/40 dp sizes as variants. Vista de erro: code builds a raw ElevatedButton and TextButton with a message in the default text style; Figma uses the Botão Primário and Texto and Corpo/Padrão text (AppButton and AppTextButton in code). Cartão de chamada: code is a Material Card with elevation 2, a bold titleLarge title, a bodySmall note in onSurface instead of color/text-secondary, a 20 dp gap before the button instead of space/sm, and a FilledButton.icon; Figma is a flat card with a color/border outline, Título/3 and the Botão Primário. Diálogo/Confiar em certificado: code uses an AlertDialog with a raw TextField and an ElevatedButton for Confiar; Figma uses the Diálogo/Confirmação shape, Campo/Texto and text buttons. The disabled card button has no Figma treatment beyond 38% opacity. MFA screens (issue #128): mfa_settings_screen.dart builds raw OutlinedButton (with icons), TextButton, CheckboxListTile and AlertDialog; Figma uses Botão Contorno and Texto (AppOutlinedButton of #101, AppTextButton), Caixa de seleção (new AppCheckbox atom) and Diálogo/Confirmação, with the disable dialog's code field between message and actions (a detached copy; Diálogo/Confirmação has no field slot). The MFA code field has a leading shield icon that Campo/Texto lacks (an icon slot on AppTextField/Campo/Texto), the secret and backup codes use a monospace titleMedium with no Figma text style, and both screens build a Material AppBar (until #169). Outlined-button icons (copy, open_in_new, share) cannot be swapped on the Figma instances.

The app lock frames (issue #127, section `1052:38698` of page 04) draw what the code does, so these are the differences and each is a code follow-up. The switch rows are `AppSwitch` (plain `SwitchListTile`), drawn as `Interruptor/Item` Ícone=Não. The grace-period choices are Material `RadioListTile`s in the theme's default colours, drawn as `Rádio/Item` (`color/primary` selected, `color/text-secondary` otherwise); code has no shared radio atom. `SettingsSectionHeader` is `titleMedium` bold in `color/primary` (16 dp); no text style matches, so the frames use `Interface/Botão` (14 dp SemiBold) in `color/primary`. The lock cover builds its title, description and error as inline `Text` (`headlineSmall`, `bodyMedium`, error in `color/danger`, or `color/text-secondary` after a cancel) and an `AppButton`; the authenticating frame shows `Botão` Primário at 60% opacity with `Ícone/loader` and no label, where code shows `AppLoadingIndicator` (20 dp, `color/on-primary`) in a disabled button. The cover uses the logo at 96 dp. The entry row in `/settings` uses `Lista/Item` with `Ícone/lock` (added in #127, Lucide style) where code uses `Icons.lock_outline`, and its description is cut to one line in Figma while the `ListTile` subtitle wraps. The Figma frames omit the SnackBar's behaviour (hidden before the next one) and the `Semantics` live regions on the cover and the unsupported text.

Material text roles Figma does not define (displayMedium, displaySmall, headlineLarge, titleMedium, titleSmall) keep Material default sizes but render in Inknut Antiqua through ThemeData.fontFamily; bodySmall and other roles use onSurface, not color/text-secondary or color/text-muted. The mapped roles also change Material default sizes globally (bodyLarge 16->18, bodyMedium 14->16, bodySmall 12->14, labelMedium 12->13, labelSmall 11->12) with 150-160% line heights, so ListTile, TextField, dialog and chip text grow; check fixed-height rows at large text scales.
radius/*, space/* and Vidro effects have no ThemeData/ThemeExtension counterpart.

GatunoColors badge colors (badgeDefault, badgeSearch, badgeType, badgeExcluded, badgeSensitive, badgePublication, badgeAuthor) and the AppColors.badge*Light constants have no Figma variable; the Figma Tag/Filtro components should be inspected before mapping.
GatunoColors.degrader gradient has no Figma style.

Figma mobile sections 3 (Library/Profile), 4 (Auth) and 5 (Settings) have frames since issue #52 (Dark theme only, key states). Still without frames: web sections 3 (Auth) and 4 (Settings), web /library and /users/:userId, and the code-only welcome and certificates screens. The MFA screens (/auth/mfa, /settings/mfa) have frames since issue #128, in their own sections on the same page (1052:38039, 1052:39164); see .impeccable/surfaces/mfa.md.

Figma routes /library, /users/:userId and /latest-reads have no matching code routes; Figma /auth/login, /auth/register, /user and /users/:userId map to code /auth/signin, /auth/signup, /settings and /settings/profile under different names. Code-only routes without Figma frames: /settings/certificates, /chapters/:id, /chapters/:id/page/:index, /requests, /requests/create and /welcome.
